given.part: An open loan's `dueOn` is before today (UTC)
given.why: Loans lent on 03-02 are due 03-16, and the clock is set to 03-17 before the job runs.

given.part: it has no reminder recorded today
given.why: The database starts empty, so no reminder exists before the run.

then.part: Asks the Notifications API to notify the loan's member
then.why: `fakeNotifications.sent` must hold exactly two entries, each with the right memberId, loanId and dueOn.

then.part: then records a reminder for today
then.why: The reminders table is asserted to hold `sent_on` 2026-03-17 for both loans.
mutants.json marks this as covered by B3, whose test shows nothing is recorded for the refused loan.

given.part: An open loan already has a reminder recorded today
given.why: The job runs twice, so the second run meets loan1 with a reminder already recorded today.
loan2 is returned before the job runs.
loan3 is lent on 03-03, so it is due exactly on 03-17, the day of the run, which tests the boundary.

then.why: After two runs, `sent` matches exactly [loan1], so the repeat, the returned loan and the not-yet-overdue loan each add nothing.

given.why: `refuseFor(loan1, ...)` makes the fake return a refusal for that loan.
B5's test maps a failed connection to a refusal. The service test only ever sees a refusal.

then.why: The reminders table is asserted to hold only loan2's row.
The assertion matches on level `warn` and event `reminder.failed`.
`objectContaining` checks only level and event, so a wrong or missing `loanId` field would still pass.
The `error` field is never asserted, so a hard-coded or missing error would pass.

then.part: carries on with the other loans
then.why: loan1, lent first, is refused and loan2 is still sent and recorded, so a break or early exit would fail.

given.part: The job has handled every overdue loan
given.why: Three overdue loans are set up, with one refused.

then.why: The last log entry is asserted with `toEqual` on level `info`, the event, and exact counts `sent` 2 and `failed` 1.

given.why: The tests call `sendOverdueReminder` with a concrete reminder.

then.why: The captured request is asserted for method POST, path /notifications and content-type application/json, against a client built on NOTIFY_URL.

then.part: body `{ memberId, template: "loan-overdue", data: { loanId, dueOn } }`
then.why: The body is asserted with exact equality.
202, 200 and 204 are each asserted as accepted.

then.part: any other answer ... as refused, with a reason naming the status
then.why: A 400 gives `refused` with a reason containing "400".

then.part: a failed connection as refused, with a reason saying the API was unreachable
then.why: A network error gives `refused` with a reason containing "unreachable".
